Zipper is a little fly character from the animated series Chip 'n Dale Rescue Rangers. A running gag in the series is that Zipper is often mistaken for an alien whenever he gets big or switches bodies with a human. Zipper is introduced together with Monterey Jack in the five-part origin story "To the Rescue".
Zafiro is a gargoyle and the leader of the Mayan Clan in the animated series Gargoyles. His name is derived from the sapphire pendant he wears.

Yubaba (湯婆婆, Yubaaba) is the proprietor of The Bathhouse and the main antagonist from Spirited Away. She is the identical twin sister of Zeniba and mother of Boh. She has a bird servant affectionately referred to by fans as Yu-Bird, an apprentice nicknamed Haku, and is the employer of countless other bathhouse workers.

A gun shield is a piece of armor designed to be mounted on a crew-served weapon such as a machine gun or artillery piece, or, more rarely, to be used with an assault rifle. During the trench warfare stage of World War I, shields with clearance for a rifle barrel were sometimes used by riflemen to more safely fire at targets in no-man's-land. Shields were sometimes also fitted to wheeled rigs to make them mobile.

Zoso, formerly known as the Dark One, is a minor antagonist of ABC's Once Upon a Time and he appears in the eighth episode of the first season. Zoso is an evil man cursed with eternal life, but gifted with powerful magical abilities. He was portrayed by Brad Dourif, who is best known as the voice of Chucky from Child's Play series.
The Zombies are minor antagonists in The Haunted Mansion. They are the undead inhabitants of the mausoleum in the graveyard near Gracey Manor.

Zoltan the Magnificent is a deleted character in Atlantis: The Lost Empire who was recruited aboard the Ulysses as a medium claiming to be able to communicate telepathically with the Atlanteans. He was intended as a counterpart to Milo and other more scientifically-minded members of the crew; however, he was cut from the final version of the movie.

Smoke Bombs are munitions designed to be dropped from aircraft to generate smoke. The applications of such a device include producing a smokescreen to block enemy line of sight or conceal friendly units, as well as to visually mark targets or locations.

Zelena, the Wicked Witch of the West is a major character in the hit ABC fantasy series Once Upon a Time. She is Regina Mills' older half-sister from Cora's affair with a gardener name Jonathan. Abandoned by her mother as a child, she wished for family love but grew envious of her half-sister getting everything she ever wanted. After training with Rumplestiltskin, in hopes of changing the past, Zelena collected ingredients to activate a time portal, but her plan has evolved. Zelena later chose to mend her sisterly bond with Regina after the birth of Robin. She is based on the character of the same name from the children's novel The Wonderful Wizard of Oz.

Yzma is the main antagonist of Disney's 2000 animated feature film The Emperor's New Groove. She is an evil sorceress and the former advisor to Emperor Kuzco. After being fired from her longstanding position, Yzma becomes obsessed with killing the emperor and usurping his throne as empress. She makes numerous attempts to do so with the aid of her dim-witted assistant, Kronk, and an arsenal of madcap potions.

Bahamutt is an enemy in Super Mario RPG: Legend of the Seven Stars. They are very large, red dragon enemies that are only encountered in Bowser's Keep. They are only summoned by Magikoopa or a Chester and can be dangerous in battle. Defeating Bahamutt results in it dropping 200 coins.

The Staghound was the British and Commonwealth name for the originally American-designed T17E1 Armored Car. In a response to a 1941 US Army requirement for a medium armored reconnaissance vehicle, Chevrolet submitted the six-wheeled T17 and four-wheeled T17E1 for approval, although US procurement of both were cancelled by December 1942 in favor of the lighter M8 Greyhound. While rejected by the US military, production would continue at the request of the British - 3,844 Staghounds were produced for them under Lend Lease. Entering service too late to contribute to the North African campaign, the Staghound first saw action in Italy in 1944, as well as in North-West Europe later on. The base variant was armed with a 37mm gun in a rotating turret, but specialist vehicles could also carry dual .50 M2 Brownings, a 57mm 6-PDR, or a 3-inch or 75mm howitzer.

Awabō is a boss fought by Wario in the Ruins at the Bottom of the sea in Wario Land II. Awabō does not appear to be a specific species, although it is a bubble with small arms who has the ability to inflate itself larger. de:King Bubble es:Awabō it:Awabō fr:Awabō

Black Hole Bowser is the villain of Space Land in Mario Party 2. He is always seen in a spaceship, which, strangely enough, is not similar to the Koopa Clown Car. At the end, the winner must battle Black Hole Bowser. Black Hole Bowser has an on-board tractor beam that takes all coins from whoever it hits. It fires every time the countdown gos from 5 to 0. This happens every time a player passes through the central part of the board, where there are four different ways to go.

Blastboxers are enemies in Super Paper Mario. They are stronger, gray and white relatives of Boomboxers. Blastboxers have boombox-shaped heads and emit powerful sound waves from it, which can be countered by Barry. Like both Boomboxers and Beepboxers, Blastboxers have high HP and can get stunned from Boomer's explosion. Unlike them, however, Blastboxers shoot six sound waves instead of the typical three.

The Grenade, hand, anti-tank No. 74, commonly referred to as the Sticky Bomb, was a British thrown explosive designed and produced during World War II. The grenade was one of several emergency anti-tank measures resulting from the British evacuation from France in 1940, during which the vast majority of its dedicated anti-tank guns were left behind. Although originally developed for the Home Guard, the weapon saw use between 1941 and 1943 by regular and commando units of Britain and the Commonwealth, as well as the French Resistance.

Chuckoroks are enemies that appear in Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga. They appear in the Chuckorok Bounce minigame of Chucklehuck Woods in the Winkle area's Winkle Colosseum Chuckoroks bear a resemblance to Octoroks from The Legend of Zelda series. Their main attack is firing a laser. During the minigame, Mario and Luigi have to bounce the balls back at them.

The Dark Ninjoe is an enemy in Super Paper Mario that can be found in rooms 64, 69, 77 and 78 of the Flopside Pit of 100 Trials. It appears as a shadow of a Ninjoe. The Dark Ninjoe is found in groups in the Pit of 100 Trials. It often throws many ninja stars at the player and is a lightning-quick foe, even faster than the Ninjerry. Its card description jokingly says this challenging foe moves "at the speed of deadly," and segues into a Chuck Norris reference ("roundhouse kick"). There is no solid strategy to defeat a Dark Ninjoe, they are very tricky to hit due to their speed though stunning it with Fleep and then jumping on it is effective. However, they have one more trick up their sleeve: The Ninjoe that is attacked might be a decoy, in fact it may do this many times until the real them appears upon being attacked. Using Dottie is also another good strategy as the heroes can attack them without being seen.

Dark Koopas are strong, purple-shelled Koopa Troopas that live in dark places underground. They appear in the first two games of the Paper Mario series. In Super Paper Mario, this role is given to a pitch-black, shadowy Koopa also called Dark Koopa, which appears in the Flopside Pit of 100 Trials.

Spread is an abstraction of various real-life conditions which can cause a weapon's round to not go where the perceived aimpoint is. When a weapon is fired, there is essentially a random chance for it to go in any direction within a small area, called the cone of fire. When the weapon is fired, the game engine may apply a slight variance in a particular direction, after which the projectile will only be affected by gravity. On many automatic-fire weapons, spread will increase the longer the trigger is depressed, making later shots less likely to hit their intended target. Spread may also be wider when firing from the hip than when aiming down sight, and may increase when the player is suppressed. Spread may be reduced while crouched or prone, although it may briefly increase while in the act of crouching or going prone. In some games, light machine guns may start with a large amount of spread that decreases over time, making LMGs more valuable for suppression and situations where they can maintain sustained fire. Sniper rifles will often have zero spread while aiming down sight, and wild spread when hip-firing. Submachine guns and Personal defense weapons will typically have tight spread when hip-firing, potentially eliminating the delay of aiming down sight. Weapon attachments may alter how much spread a weapon has, or the rate at which spread recovers over time.

The Dark Tileoid is the most powerful member of the Tileoid family and an enemy in Super Paper Mario. This pitch black, shady creature is encountered only in the Flopside Pit of 100 Trials, on floors 57, 63, and 77. The Dark Tileoid moves across the floors, walls, and ceilings, only changing direction when it bumps into the player. It is faster than Tileoid Y, has more HP than Tileoid R, and has higher Attack than any other variation.
Dhalsim is an Indian yoga master from the Street Fighter franchise.
Dr. Sheldon, most often simply called Sheldon, is an elderly man who is known to be a mysterious, powerful witch doctor. He only appears in The Super Mario Bros. Super Show! episode "Jungle Fever".

Staff Cars are automobiles used by senior officers or other important personnel of a country's military force. They are non-combat vehicles that are usually modified versions of civilian cars, although light military vehicles such as the Willys MB were often used to fulfil this role. The term was applicable to the First and Second World Wars, however the distinction has become redundant today as modern day military forces are generally fully motorised.

Duplighosts are ghost-like creatures that can take on the appearance, voice and abilities of other people. They appear primarily as enemies in Paper Mario, with only a notable one appearing in Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door. To attack, Duplighosts can either fly into Mario, or turn into his current partner; in this guise, the Duplighost gains that partner's basic single-target attack and physical properties (e.g., a Duplighost turned into Watt damages Mario or his partner with Electro Dash, and hurts them if they make contact with it). Their name is a portmanteau of "duplicate" and "ghost".

The Eye Beamers (also called Scanners) are robotic enemies that appear in Super Mario Galaxy. They appear in a couple Galaxies and omit very powerful lasers that are capable of shocking their targets.
